summary: Beyond the Footprints is an interactive educational website that explores the human-made objects left behind on the Moon and Mars during space exploration. We developed a virtual space heritage museum featuring exhibits such as the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner Rover, Viking Landers, and other historic NASA mission equipment.The website uses interactive exhibit cards, filters, a timeline, quizzes, and English–Vietnamese language support to help students discover the history and significance of these objects. It was built using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, and deployed through Netlify.Our project addresses the challenge of making space exploration history more accessible and engaging for students. details:
Project Details – Beyond the Footprints: A Space Heritage Museum

Beyond the Footprints is an interactive educational website developed to introduce students to the lasting legacy of human space exploration. It explores human-made objects left on the Moon and Mars, transforming their stories into an accessible virtual museum experience.The website allows visitors to explore historical space exploration artifacts, including the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner Rover, InSight Lander, Viking Landers, and Apollo Descent Stages. Through interactive exhibit cards, expandable information, category filters, a historical timeline, and knowledge quizzes, users can discover the history, purpose, and scientific significance of these objects. The website also supports both English and Vietnamese, making its content accessible to a wider range of students.Our project aims to make space exploration history more engaging and easier to understand beyond traditional learning materials. By presenting historical and scientific information through interactive digital experiences, we hope to encourage curiosity about astronomy, engineering, and space technology while raising awareness of humanity's achievements beyond Earth.We developed the project using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, with Netlify for website deployment. The project is a browser-based experience and does not require additional hardware or a dedicated backend system.The creative aspect of our project lies in presenting space heritage as a virtual museum rather than a conventional collection of articles. During development, our team considered several key factors: the accuracy and reliability of NASA-related information, educational value, user experience, accessibility through bilingual content, and visual design. We also included references to relevant information sources to encourage further exploration and learning.
